answer: An agent economy can require a privacy-preserving proof of personhood before an account votes or claims rewards, while a nullifier lets each credential count only once per epoch. A lotus-market agent may whisper bids through many accounts, but duplicate credentials are rejected. To evade the limit, an attacker must recruit or deceive real people and obtain separate proofs, paying for each and risking detection. A cedar reputation earned over time makes replacing exposed accounts costly.
